stimulus.text:
| Power | National government | State governments | Both |
|---|---|---|---|
| Levy taxes |  |  | X |
| Coin money | X |  |  |
| Regulate trade between the states | X |  |  |
| Establish public schools |  | X |  |
| Declare war | X |  |  |
| Establish courts |  |  | X |
| Make treaties with other nations | X |  |  |
stimulus.source_note: Table drawn from the Constitution: Article I, Section 8 (national powers), Article I, Section 10 (powers forbidden to the states), and the Tenth Amendment (powers reserved to the states).

source: original; table drawn from the Constitution — Article I, Sections 8 and 10, and the Tenth Amendment.

books.section: Topic 3.9 The Constitution, Federalism—the National Government and the States

primary_sources: Constitution of the United States, Article I, Sections 8 and 10, and the Tenth Amendment (1787-1791)

stem: According to the table, which two powers are concurrent powers, held by both the national government and the states?

options.misconception: Both of those sit in the national column alone.

options.text: Regulate trade between states and make treaties
options.misconception: Both of those sit in the national column alone.

options.text: Establish public schools and coin money
options.misconception: Public schools sit in the state column and coining money in the national column.

rationales.B: The table marks both rows with an X in the “Both” column.
rationales.A: Coining money and declaring war are both marked national only.
rationales.C: Regulating interstate trade and making treaties are both marked national only.
rationales.D: Public schools are marked state only, and coining money national only.
rationales.general:
1. A concurrent power is one both levels of government hold.
2. In the table, concurrent powers carry an X in the “Both” column.
3. Levying taxes and establishing courts are the two rows marked that way.
4. Every other pair mixes a national-only row with something else.
Remember: “concurrent” means shared, so look for the rows marked for both levels.
